clue.text: Impressed women in the main when reversing vehicle

indicators.note: one thing sitting inside another is placed within it, so one piece goes inside the other
to reverse is to run backwards, so the combined letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the main is an old poetic word for the open sea
W is the standard abbreviation for women
a truck is a goods vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone is impressed by women out at sea in a vehicle that is backing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old poetic term for the open ocean, a convention worth learning; 'when' merely joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone filled with wonder and admiration is deeply impressed, which is exactly what being awestruck describes.

clue.text: Saying nothing after team splits before noon

indicators.note: coming after means following in sequence, so the second piece is placed behind the first
to split something is to break it open, so one part is wedged into the middle of another

blocks.note: a.m. stands for ante meridiem, the hours before noon
a cricket or football team has eleven players, written XI in Roman numerals
O looks like zero, meaning nothing

explanation.surface: A quiet player stays silent after the team breaks up for the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: Team as eleven in Roman numerals is a staple convention; the team plus nothing together splits the abbreviation for morning.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is an accepted truth or maxim, the same kind of thing as a proverb or familiar saying.

clue.text: Married couple overwhelmed by European welcome

indicators.note: in a down entry, being overwhelmed by something means lying beneath it, so this part sits lower in the column

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
M is the abbreviation for married, as on forms
a brace is a pair, as in a brace of pheasants

explanation.surface: A newly married pair receive a warm reception from a fellow European.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the European comes on top, with the married couple below it.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace an idea or a guest is to accept it gladly, so as verbs the two words share the sense of greeting warmly.

clue.text: Spanish accent brightened up hollow discourse

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom of the column, so the letters run backwards
something hollow has its inside scooped out, leaving just the outer shell of the word

blocks.note: lit means lit up or brightened
only the first and last letters of discourse are kept

explanation.surface: A cheerful Spanish lilt livens up an otherwise empty conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spanish accent' sounds like a way of speaking, but it is the written diacritic mark; 'up' only works because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The tilde is the wavy mark placed over the n in Spanish words such as señor, a written accent rather than a pronunciation.

clue.text: Weird, upper-class childminder steals redcoat's heart

indicators.note: the heart of something is its centre, so only the middle letter of the word is used
a thief who steals takes something into their possession, so one piece ends up held inside the other

blocks.note: U is the classic label for upper-class usage
a nanny looks after children
the middle letter of this seven-letter word

explanation.surface: A strange posh nanny pinches the affections of a British soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside NANNY after its first letter, and U comes in front. A redcoat was a British soldier, from the red uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncanny describes something strange in an unsettling, mysterious way, a close synonym of weird.

clue.text: Provide stimulus to quit celebrity contest's final

indicators.note: the final part of something is its end, so only the last letter is taken

blocks.note: to kick a habit is to quit it
a celebrity is a star
the last letter of contest

explanation.surface: Someone is spurred into walking out of the last round of a celebrity show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quit' means kick only in the sense of kicking a habit; KICK, STAR and T join in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To kick-start something is to give it an initial boost or impetus to get it moving, as with a motorbike engine.

clue.text: Religious teaching bishop found on carbon copy

indicators.note: being found on something means coming right after it, so the pieces line up one after another

blocks.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
RI is religious instruction, the old school subject
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop's religious lesson turns out to be written on a carbon copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carbon copy' looks like one phrase, but carbon is the element and copy is the definition. RI is religious instruction, a British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: To crib is to copy someone else's work dishonestly, as a pupil might in an exam.

clue.text: Switzerland enraged over new heraldic device

indicators.note: something enraged is in a wild state, so the following letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: The Swiss are furious about a new coat-of-arms design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' looks like part of 'enraged over', but it is anagram material along with N. CH, for Confoederatio Helvetica, is Switzerland's country code.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a chevron is an inverted V-shaped band on a shield, one of the standard charges or devices.

clue.text: Part of shoe pinching enclosed nerve

indicators.note: to pinch is to grip tightly, so one piece holds another clamped inside it

blocks.note: the insole is the inner sole of a shoe
enc. is the abbreviation for enclosed, used on letters

explanation.surface: A tight shoe nips a nerve in the foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nerve' looks anatomical in the surface but is the cheek sense; 'enclosed' is the abbreviation written at the foot of business letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the nerve to do something means showing cheek or impudence, which is rude disrespect, i.e. insolence.

clue.text: Infernal odour permeates laid-back island clubs

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the word is read from right to left
to permeate is to spread through the inside of something, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: taken as written
BO is body odour
I is the abbreviation for island
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A hellish smell hangs over the nightclubs of a relaxed holiday island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid-back' reads as relaxed, but it splits into a word and its direction signal; the island and clubs then supply single letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Infernal relates to hell, and diabolic means devilish or of the devil, so both describe wicked hellish things.

clue.text: Clothing line?

blocks.note: surface reading: a range of garments sold by a fashion brand
setter's reading: a line pressed or folded into a garment

explanation.walkthrough: A clothing line sounds like a designer's range of garments, but the setter means a literal line in clothing, such as one pressed into trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: A fold mark ironed or wrinkled into fabric runs as a straight line across the garment, so it is literally a line on clothes.

clue.text: Spike Lee endlessly hounds politician in Iowa

indicators.note: being in a place means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other
without an end means the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: IA is the postal abbreviation for the US state
MP is Member of Parliament
the name without its last letter

explanation.surface: Film director Spike Lee pursues a politician in Iowa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spike Lee' looks like the American film director's name, but Spike is the definition, and 'hounds' is only a link joining the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: To spike something is to pierce it on a sharp point, which is what impaling does.

clue.text: King captivated by cuts on revolutionary's facial features

indicators.note: a revolution turns things right round, so these letters are read backwards
being captivated by something means being held captive by it, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: slits are narrow cuts
taken as written
R is for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch is charmed by the scars on a revolutionary's face.
explanation.walkthrough: The turnaround applies to both 'cuts' and 'on' together before the king is captured; R for rex is a standard convention.
explanation.definitionFit: The two openings of the nose are features of the face, so they fit a general description of facial parts.

clue.text: Ease off drug following essentially miserable period of abstinence

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so only the central letter is taken
following means coming after, so one piece is placed behind another

blocks.note: the middle letter of this nine-letter word
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
Lent is the forty days before Easter when Christians give things up

explanation.surface: Someone comes off drugs after a miserable stretch of going without.
explanation.walkthrough: E follows the middle letter of 'miserable', then LENT completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to soften or slacken in severity, which is what easing off a harsh stance means.

clue.text: English queen put on international food fair

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting one thing on another means stacking it above, so the pieces run top to bottom

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
Qu is an abbreviation for queen
I is the abbreviation for international
table means the food served, as in keeping a good table

explanation.surface: An English queen lays on a spread at an international food festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Food fair' reads as one event, but fair is the definition on its own; table in the sense of the meals provided supplies TABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Equitable means just and impartial, treating everyone evenly, which is the adjective sense of fair.

clue.text: Reprimand resulting from crooked tag on kilt

indicators.note: something crooked is bent out of shape, so the letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Scotsman is told off because the label on his kilt hangs askew.
explanation.walkthrough: The three words supply exactly nine letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A talking-to is a scolding or telling-off, an informal word for a reprimand.

clue.text: Fancy letters initially ignored by Yankee

indicators.note: the initial is the first letter, and ignoring it means leaving it out

blocks.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet
letters means learning, as in a man of letters, minus its first letter

explanation.surface: Elaborate lettering gets passed over by an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy letters' suggests ornate script, but letters means scholarship, LEARNING. Dropping L and adding Y in front gives YEARNING.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a fancy to something is a longing or desire for it, so as nouns both mean a strong wish.

clue.text: Foul salt on the rocks where sewage pipes emerge

indicators.note: something on the rocks is wrecked, so the letters are smashed and reassembled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Dirty salty water washes over the rocks at the end of the sewer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the rocks' fits the seaside scene, but it is the signal to rearrange; the first two words supply the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfall is the mouth of a drain or sewer, the point where it discharges into the sea or a river.

clue.text: Cautiously approach hooligan with prior charge

indicators.note: something prior comes earlier, so this piece is placed in front of the other

blocks.note: a fee is a charge for a service
a lout is a rough yob

explanation.surface: Police edge carefully towards a thug who already has a criminal record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prior charge' suggests a criminal record, but charge is just a fee placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel someone out is to sound out their views tentatively, testing the ground before committing.

clue.text: Staff worked out secret about head of production

indicators.note: the head of something is its top, so the first letter is taken
a puzzle worked out has been sorted and rearranged, so the letters change order
about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of production

explanation.surface: Employees have uncovered a secret concerning the boss of a production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like the workers, but it is a rod. SECRET rearranged wraps around P.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptre is the ornamental rod a monarch carries, a ceremonial kind of staff or stick.

clue.text: Discovered articles for every mood

indicators.note: dis-covered means with its cover taken off, so the outside letters are stripped away

blocks.note: items, articles, with first and last letters removed
per means for each, as in per person

explanation.surface: Items have been found to suit any frame of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' looks like found, but it means stripped of covering: ITEMS loses its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Temper means a state of mind or disposition, as in being in a good temper, so it is a synonym of mood.

clue.text: Is bothered by extremely elitist attitude

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only those letters are kept

blocks.note: if someone minds, they are bothered or object
the first and last letters of elitist

explanation.surface: Someone is irritated by a very snobbish attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is bothered' becomes the single word MINDS; the ends of 'elitist' follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A mindset is an established way of thinking or outlook, much the same as an attitude.

clue.text: Put under pressure, archaeologist ultimately unveiled treasure alongside earl

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the last letter of each preceding word is taken
to unveil is to strip away the covering, so the outside letters are dropped
alongside means next to, so this piece is placed beside the rest

blocks.note: the last letter of pressure
the last letter of archaeologist
to treasure is to cherish, minus its first and last letters
E is the abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: Under strain, an archaeologist finally reveals a treasure found beside a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put under pressure' looks like one phrase, but the definition is 'Put under', and 'ultimately' takes the ends of both pressure and archaeologist.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone under is to anaesthetise them, and etherising means doing so using ether, the early anaesthetic gas.

clue.text: Door in castle regularly decorated

indicators.note: doing something regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A castle door is ornamented at intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the even letters of the first three words spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ornate is elaborately adorned, so it is highly decorated.

clue.text: Australia working with Spain to produce natural sunscreen

blocks.note: Oz is the informal name for Australia
a machine that is on is working
E is the international code for Spain

explanation.surface: Australia and Spain team up to develop a natural sun cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Natural sunscreen' sounds like a product, but it is the gas layer high in the atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: The ozone layer in the upper atmosphere absorbs much of the sun's ultraviolet radiation, shielding the Earth like a natural filter.

clue.text: Spells words

blocks.note: first meaning: fixed periods of time, such as stints in office
second meaning: words or expressions, as in technical vocabulary

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spells words' suggests spelling out words, but spells means periods of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A school or office period is a fixed stretch of time, while the same word also means a name or expression for something.

clue.text: Old water pipe retains L-shape

indicators.note: to retain is to keep hold of, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a bong is a water pipe for smoking
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old plumbing pipe keeps its L-shaped bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'L-shape' looks like one thing, but the L is a letter and shape alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblong is a rectangle longer than it is wide, a familiar geometric figure.

clue.text: Model wakes up with runs in legwear

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: the Model T was Henry Ford's famous car
to rouse someone is to wake them
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A model wakes to find ladders in her tights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs in legwear' suggests ladders in stockings, but the R just goes inside ROUSES. Model gives T via the Model T Ford.
explanation.definitionFit: Trousers are garments covering each leg separately, so they are a kind of clothing for the legs.

clue.text: Son boarding plane makes joke

indicators.note: a passenger boarding goes on board, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a jet is an aeroplane
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A boy getting on an aircraft cracks a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes inside JET.
explanation.definitionFit: A jest is a light-hearted remark meant to amuse, a slightly old-fashioned word for a joke.

clue.text: Allow time on vacation to partake in some exotic meals

indicators.note: something vacated has been emptied, so only the outside letters of the word stay
exotic means strange and foreign, so the letters are rearranged into an unfamiliar form
to partake in something is to take part inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: to allow is to let
the first and last letters of time
taken as written

explanation.surface: On holiday, someone allows time to sample unusual foreign dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' looks like being on holiday, but it means emptied, so the word for time loses its middle before joining the permission word.
explanation.definitionFit: Omelettes are egg dishes eaten for lunch or supper, so each one is an example of a meal.
